title: Fix a broken regex validation
description: validate_email() in validators.py uses an unescaped '.' before the TLD, so the regex '.' metacharacter matches ANY character, not just a literal dot. This means strings with no real domain dot (e.g. 'bob@sitexcom') are incorrectly accepted. Escape the dot (and tighten the TLD to letters) so only real email-shaped strings validate.
